articles.title: Jayson Tatum Discusses Jaylen Brown Trade, Relationship in New Video, Former Celtics Teammate Reacts
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum said he was stunned when he first learned over the summer that Jaylen Brown had been traded to the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum said he was stunned when he first learned over the summer that Jaylen Brown had been traded to the Philadelphia 76ers.

"We was in Vegas. I just got done playing pickup the first day," he said on a video on his YouTube channel. "[ESPN's Shams Charania] walked over. He handed me the towel. He's like, 'Yo, put this over your face. Don't react. They just traded him.' I'm like, 'Oh s--t.' I'm like, 'Where?' He said, 'Philly.' I said, 'We traded him down the street?' So, I was just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world."

Brown responded to Tatum's reaction with a cap emoji, indicating that he thinks his former teammate isn't telling the truth about the situation.

In the video, Tatum went on to speak about what his time with Brown in Boston meant to him.

"I've very much have been transparent about how thankful I personally am for our relationship and what we were able to accomplish over nine years," he said. "Talk about 2017-26. Jayson and Jaylen, like you won't ever be able to talk about one of us without the other. And you know just our ability to grow up as kids and go through our ups and downs and people talking about, one of us had to go, and we couldn't win together. And just, there's a lot of s--t that we had to deal with, and I will always say I knew every time I stepped on that court that, when it was time to go to war, I looked to my left and to my right and No. 7 was over there. I knew that he was going to do whatever it took for us to to win. You know the way that we pushed each other, I definitely made him better and he made me better. And we made our team better. We made this organization better. We won a championship. Like we were forever stitched in stone in NBA history. We held up that trophy. It won't ever be forgotten."

The Celtics traded Brown to the Sixers for Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks over the summer. While there were rumblings that a trade could go down, sending Brown to a rival came as a pretty huge surprise.

articles.title: ESPN ranks the WNBA's greatest players of all time; 6 UConn stars make the list
articles.summary: Two of ESPN's top three WNBA players ever starred at UConn; six former Huskies made the Top 30 list.
articles.body:
The WNBA's 30th season is coming to a close with a Finals matchup featuring plenty of UConn women's basketball representation, as four former Huskies play for the Golden State Valkyries.

To commemorate the occasion, ESPN released a list of the 30 greatest stars to ever play in the WNBA over the past three decades, also dotted with Geno Auriemma products. Here's a look at the six former UConn players on ESPN's list:

Over a glittering two-decade WNBA career, Diana Taurasi shattered the league's all-time scoring record by more than 2,000 points along with several other notable records: she's also first in scoring titles and playoff points, and tied for second in All-Star selections. For many years, this statistical dominance often made her a popular choice as the WNBA's greatest-ever player, but the recent rise of A'ja Wilson, who won her third consecutive MVP award this season, led ESPN to rank the Aces star at No. 1.

"Think of any basketball superlative and it applies to Taurasi," ESPN's Charlie Creme writes. "Tough. A winner. Clutch. Unrelenting. Brilliant as a shooter, passer and playmaker. She won big. She scored big. She played big. She has always been the player no one could take their eyes off of."

Moore squeezed a tremendous amount of winning into her relatively short eight-year playing career, winning four WNBA championships as she helped elevate the Minnesota Lynx into the league's gold standard under Cheryl Reeve. Her most statistically impressive season came in 2014, averaging nearly 24 points, eight rebounds and 3.4 assists en route to her only MVP award.

"Moore is the one player on this list for whom fans will forever ask, 'What if?' Her career was short by superstar standards," ESPN writes. "But those eight years before she stepped away to help fight for criminal justice reform were just so good."

Breanna Stewart is the only active UConn alum on ESPN's list and is still doing quite a bit to further her WNBA legacy after a decade in the league. The Liberty power forward finished fifth in MVP voting in 2026, adding to a decorated résumé that includes two MVP awards, eight All-Star appearances and three WNBA titles.

"With her 6-4 frame and 7-1 wingspan to go along with guard-level ball-handling skills and deep shooting range, Stewart might be the most physically distinctive player the WNBA has ever seen," ESPN writes. "She runs the floor brilliantly but can also lead a break. There isn't a position on the court she can't guard or an area of the game she can't influence."

Bird partnered with Taurasi for two seasons in UConn's backcourt before also heading west to start a career defined by longevity and loyalty. Across two decades with the Seattle Storm, Bird set all-time marks in career assists and games played that still hold up, resulting in 13 All-Star appearances, eight All-WNBA selections and four WNBA titles.

"It might seem unfair that Bird isn't in the top 10, but it reflects something in which point guards take pride: making everyone around them better," ESPN writes. "The player right ahead of Bird on this list, longtime Storm teammate Lauren Jackson, would attest to that. No one played more WNBA games or was more respected as a leader than the Seattle icon, who has a statue outside Climate Pledge Arena."

After a standout college tenure in Storrs, Tina Charles began a similarly accomplished WNBA career just down the road at Mohegan Sun Arena, earning two first-team All-WNBA selections and an MVP award over four seasons after the Connecticut Sun selected her No. 1 overall. Charles remained one of the WNBA's premier players across six more seasons with the New York Liberty, and in the twilight of her career, she bounced between several teams before returning to Connecticut and retiring with the Sun last season.

"A dominant force from the day she stepped onto a WNBA court, Charles was the epitome of reliability and productivity until her retirement in May," ESPN writes.

Cash enjoyed a tremendous, 15-year WNBA career primarily with the now-defunct Detroit Shock and the Seattle Storm, earning four All-Star appearances and three WNBA titles. She might still have a chance to build on her WNBA legacy a decade after retirement, with Cash considered an early contender to replace outgoing league commissioner Cathy Engelbert ahead of the 2027 season.

"Cash was never on the first team for All-WNBA or defense," ESPN writes. "Yet she is a player who could change games with her effort and energy, along with her talent."

articles.title: Caleb Wilson takes humbling lesson from getting crushed in NBA debut
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Caleb Wilson got his feet wet in his debut with the Chicago Bulls. However, the Bulls suffered a historic blowout loss to the Toronto Raptors,...
articles.body:
On Wednesday, Caleb Wilson got his feet wet in his debut with the Chicago Bulls . However, the Bulls suffered a historic blowout loss to the Toronto Raptors, 135-92.

Wilson finished the game with 16 points and 4 rebounds. But he also had 9 turnovers.

After the game, Wilson took it stride as a learning process, per Bulls on CHSN.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I just feel like it's a learning lesson," Wilson said.

He also took responsibility for the turnovers, committed himself to correcting his mistakes, and looked ahead to the next game.

Wilson's maturity has already endeared him to those who expect nothing but the best from him. The No. 4 draft pick out of North Carolina has to shoulder the burden of carrying the Bulls from the doldrums of the NBA back to some semblance of legitimacy.

Undoubtedly, Wilson's ascendancy has become a focal point for an organization in the midst of a top-down rebuild.

He's already shown his potential preparation for his first season. In the NBA Summer League, Wilson made the All-Summer League First Team , averaging 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 2.5 blocks. In the preseason, Wilson was on top of his game . He averaged 15.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game.

Wilson's on-court talent, combined with his leadership, makes him a strong candidate for NBA Rookie of the Year.

The Bulls will travel to Milwaukee to play against the Bucks on Friday night. It was added to make way for Game 1 of the World Series. Then, they will play in their home opener against the Washington Wizards on Saturday night.

articles.title: How Zion Williamson ‘respectfully’ processed latest loss amid questions about Pelicans’ future with Jeremiah Fears
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans have heard the promises before. New coach, renewed expectations, flashes of potential, and another opportunity to turn the corner. Z...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans have heard the promises before. New coach, renewed expectations, flashes of potential, and another opportunity to turn the corner. Zion Williamson has lived through enough of those cycles to know that optimism means little without results. A three-point, last-second opening night loss to Tyrese Haliburton's Indiana Pacers (123-120) was another frustrating reminder of how difficult it has been to translate talent into victories.

Williamson is not abandoning hope after one game under Jamahl Mosley . However, the two-time All-Star is no longer interested in pretending that being competitive is the same as becoming a contender.

"I can't even say…" Williamson told ClutchPoints before pivoting. "I feel like we are right there, like we are going to make that turn (under Mosley), but it's tough saying it when, respectfully, I feel like we've dealt with that in the past two to three years. And I've said it before, it's hard to win in this league. So if we want to win, (closing games) is a hurdle we've just got to get over."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That carefully chosen "respectfully" revealed plenty about Williamson's mindset. He believes in Mosley's vision but understands the skepticism surrounding a franchise that has repeatedly struggled to turn promising performances into sustained success. The comments reflected both hope and realism about a core that has repeatedly hovered near the Play-In Tournament line in recent seasons only to fall short, leaving the franchise stuck in the NBA's purgatory of mediocrity cycle.

Rebuilding around the 'next' future is becoming an unignorable option with every loss.

Adapting to the NBA is rarely a smooth transition. Fears found out about the humiliation that comes with those very public growing pains firsthand in last year's season opener against Ja Morant. Williamson defended the then-rookie following a loss to the Memphis Grizzlies last October, and provided some new notes after losing to Tyrese Haliburton's Indiana Pacers to open up Year Two together.

Fears came back into this season ready to be the future, the face of the Pelicans going forward. Williamson will have the 20-year-old's back every step of the way.

"Oh yeah, (Fears) is going to stand his ground," Williamson smiled. "And I told him, 'as long as I'm out there with you, you're good man. Do whatever. Get in people's heads. Whatever it is, I'm going to be right there with you. I'm going to protect you.' So, that's just the energy he brings to the game and, not just to the game, that's who he is as a person. Like, he is a competitor who just wants to win. I've said it before, and I'll say it again that I'm glad he is with us."

Williamson's message after losing to Tyrese Haliburton was unmistakable. The Pelicans cannot keep celebrating how close they are to a corner. Eventually, they have to make the turn. If Fears and Missi are truly the future in New Orleans, the responsibility for making that future different begins with the veterans surrounding them today. And that bit of insight comes from the other All-Star on the team, Dejounte Murray.

articles.title: Knicks superfans give baby ultimate name in honor of team's NBA championship win
articles.summary: The New York Knicks won their first NBA championship in 53 years.
articles.body:
This New York Knicks couple went above and beyond to celebrate the team's NBA championship win by naming their newborn son after the historic event.

When the Knicks clinched the title, Yvonne Gonzalez-Bradford was seven months pregnant, and she and her husband Vance Bradford already had names picked out for their bundle of joy. The couple decided on Lady Victoria if the baby was a girl, and Prestige Wisdom if the baby was a boy.

The city came alive after the Knicks won over the San Antonio Spurs in five games of the seven-game series, where there was nowhere in New York you couldn't hear ecstatic fans cheering, "Knicks in 5!"

Vance told Today.com that it sparked an idea to potentially change the name of their son as he asked his wife, "What if we give our son a name for a champion? What about Knickson?'"

Yvonne was on board, and Vance revealed that the name would be special not only to honor the Knicks winning the championship but because his family has been die-hard fans for years.

Two days later, Yvonne suggested Fyve as a middle name to reference the number of games that the Knicks won to bring home the title.

"You know how when something happens so well in your favor, you don't want to jinx it?" Vance says, recounting how excited he was to hear his wife's suggestion. "I was just like, 'Yep! Absolutely. That's it!'"

Vance added another layer to his son's name sharing, "The Roman numeral for five is 'V,' like my name, so he's named after me in a way. Five is also an indivisible number. So he's our indivisible champion. You can hear him cooing in the background right now."

Knickson Fyve was born on August 8, 2026, which is also significant to his mother, as he was welcomed into the world on Yvonne's birthday.

The couple has already been asked what will happen if Knickson decides to be a fan of another NBA team in the future.

"If he turns out to be a Celtics fan or a Sixers fan, again he's still Knickson Bradford, who is in the boardroom," Vance humorously says. "We wanted to have a very strong and firm name that would lead to a cool life. Knickson Fyve is definitely our motto. Knickson Fyve forever!"

The Knicks just finished their first regular-season game against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 20. Before tip-off, the banner was raised to showcase their championship win as well as be awarded with their rings.

Unfortunately for the reigning NBA champions, they lost their home opener 100-106, but there is still more than enough time to get right back in rhythm.

The next game for the Knicks will be against the Boston Celtics on Friday, Oct. 23 at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton moved to tears after long-awaited return from Achilles injury
articles.summary: Tyrese Halliburton was moved to tears after returning from his Achilles injury, then scored 16 fourth-quarter points to lift the Pacers past the Pelicans.
articles.body: Nearly 500 days had passed since Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton last played in a regular-season NBA game. On Wednesday, the two-time All-Star made his long-awaited return, scoring 23 points to help Indiana secure a 123-120 season-opening victory over the New Orleans Pelicans. Haliburton was sidelined for the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn Achilles tendon suffered during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. The Oklahoma City Thunder went on to win the championship that year. During Wednesday’s on-court postgame interview, the conversation took an emotional turn as Haliburton reflected on his long road back to the hardwood. INDIANA PACERS' STAR TYRESE HALIBURTON HAS ONE MAJOR PROBLEM WITH THE NEW NBA SCHEDULE Asked about his performance in the season opener and how much fun he had playing with his teammates, Haliburton became visibly emotional. "It means a lot to be back out here," Haliburton said as he fought back tears. "We've got a lot to pick up, the second quarter wasn't good. But, we're battle-tested so we finished this game the right way. Just really proud of this group." Haliburton added: "... I’m just really thankful to be back out here." PACERS' TYRESE HALIBURTON TALKS SHINGLES BATTLE AS HE RECOVERS FROM TORN ACHILLES Haliburton came through in the closing minutes, making a key play that put the Pacers ahead for good after they had trailed by as many as 10 points. Haliburton was particularly productive in the final quarter Wednesday, scoring 16 of his 23 points in that period. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Pacers experienced a significant drop-off without their star guard last season, finishing with just 19 wins. That was a far cry from the team that had come within one victory of winning an NBA championship the year before. With Haliburton back, Indiana expects to contend in a competitive Eastern Conference. The Pacers host the Dallas Mavericks on Friday for their home opener.

articles.title: Watch LeBron James Give VJ Edgecombe Bloody Nose After 76ers Teammates Collide in Viral Video
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James accidentally gave teammate VJ Edgecombe a bloody nose while the two were going for a defensive rebound in the third quarter of their home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday evening.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James accidentally gave teammate VJ Edgecombe a bloody nose while the two were going for a defensive rebound in the third quarter of their home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday evening.

To start the sequence, Cavaliers center Jarrett Allen missed a free throw with four minutes left in the frame. Cleveland guard Donovan Mitchell initially pushed James from behind in the battle for the board, leading to a loose ball foul call.

As James went up in the air, his left arm connected with Edgecombe's nose.

Thankfully, this was much ado about nothing, and Edgecombe was able to stay in the game after taking care of the matter. James also hit a pair of free throws following the foul call.

After the game, Edgecombe spoke on the matter and even joked about it.

As for the game, the 76ers overcame a 69-45 halftime deficit to win 114-106 and move to 2-0 on the season.

articles.title: 76ers Beat Cavs After Epic Comeback, Box Score Stats, Highlights for LeBron, Harden, Brown, More
articles.summary: There is no doubt that the Philadelphia 76ers are loaded with talent. Turns out they're already pretty resilient, too.
articles.body:
There is no doubt that the Philadelphia 76ers are loaded with talent. Turns out they're already pretty resilient, too.

The Sixers overcame a 29-point first-half deficit on Thursday, defeating the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 while thrilling the Philly fans in the team's home opener.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

The Cavaliers were all over the Sixers early, racing out to a 35-18 lead after the first quarter and a 69-45 margin at halftime. They led by as many as 29 points in the second quarter.

But the Sixers roared back in the third, outscoring the Cavs by a 37-21 margin and at one point cut the deficit to just two points. That set the stage for an exciting fourth quarter.

But the Sixers had figured something out and continued to frustrate the Cavaliers with relentless defense, transition scoring and individual brilliance in the halfcourt.

It was a similar theme on Tuesday night, when the Sixers hit a different gear in the second half and beat the defending-champion New York Knicks. It's a promising start for a group that's barely played together, even if there are some issues to work out (slow starts, disjoined halfcourt offense at times, turnovers, etc.).

But beating two genuine Eastern Conference contenders to open the 2026-27 campaign is gonna have an already-buzzing Philadelphia feeling pretty optimistic. For now, any concerns about how the pieces would fit have been allayed.

articles.title: 76ers rally from 29-point deficit for biggest comeback of LeBron James' career to win home opener over Cavs, 114-106
articles.summary: Philadelphia outscored Cleveland 69-37 in the second half, the team's largest comeback in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98).
articles.body:
The new-look Philadelphia 76ers staged a thrilling comeback for the home crowd in their regular-season home opener. Trailing by 29 points in the first half, the Sixers rode a second-half surge for a 38-point swing and an eventual 114-106 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday.

The comeback was the biggest of LeBron James' 24-year NBA career, making his home debut a memorable one. Previously, he was 0-52 when behind by 29 points or more.

Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points with six assists, followed by 24 points and seven rebounds from Joel Embiid to lead Philadelphia. Jaylen Brown added 21 points with eight boards, while James added 17 points with 9 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals.

Teams that had a lead of 20+points at halftime were 65-0 in their season openers since the shot-clock era began in 1954-55, according to ESPN. The Cavaliers had a 155-0 record with a 29-point lead, while the 76ers were 0-156 facing such a deficit.

Overall, NBA teams had won 466 consecutive games with that kind of lead during the regular season, the Associated Press' Tim Reynolds reported.

Philadelphia took its first lead of the game at 96-95 five minutes into the fourth quarter on seven straight points by Embiid. Brown followed with a long fadeaway jumper, a driving layup between two defenders and a midrange shot to put Philadelphia ahead by seven points.

The Sixers came out strong to begin the third quarter, scoring 11 points in the opening 90 seconds to cut the Cavs' lead to 13 points. Donovan Mitchell got two baskets to slow Philadelphia down, but that was temporary as Philadelphia kept up a quicker pace.

A fast-break layup and 3-pointer from Maxey made it an 80-73 Cavs lead at the five-minute mark of the quarter. That got the crowd back on the home team's side, chanting "trust the process" as the deficit was reduced to five points.

Perhaps the most important point of the game for Philadelphia was a two-minute stretch late in the third quarter when head coach Nick Nurse gave Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid a rest. The Cavs weren't able to capitalize, but did manage to push their lead back up to 90-82 when Maxey and Brown came back in toward the end of the quarter.

Playing their first game of the season, the Cavaliers seemed determined to show that last season's Eastern Conference finalists won't just step aside and let the Sixers cruise to the NBA Finals unchallenged.

Despite a night off since Tuesday's season-opening win over the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks, Philadelphia initially played like a team that left all of its energy at Madison Square Garden. Maybe the effort to upstage the Knicks when they received their championship rings and establish their place in the East's hierarchy set a level difficult to match early on.

After Maxey hit a short jumper to tie the score at 11-11, the Cavaliers went on a 12-0 run. That eventually became a 24-7 surge to end the first quarter. The margin didn't shrink during the second quarter, with Cleveland outscoring the Sixers 34-27 to take a 24-point lead and prompt boos from the Xfinity Mobile Center crowd into halftime. And that was with Embiid hitting a 3-pointer just before the buzzer.

During "Inside the NBA" before the game, Charles Barkley expressed his concern that Philadelphia's obvious weakness is its lack of size besides Embiid. Cleveland made Barkley look prescient with Evan Mobley (15 first-half points) and Jarrett Allen (14) dominating in the frontcourt while playing Embiid tough. The 76ers' center had nine points on 3-of-10 shooting at the half.

Mitchell finished with 32 points and 10 rebounds to lead the Cavs. However, he missed two free throws with 1:19 remaining in regulation that could have pulled Cleveland to within two points.

James Harden scored 16 points with five assists. But Mobley scored only three points in the second half and Allen went scoreless.

Joel Embiid and LeBron James break out new pregame handshake

By halftime, it appeared that the most memorable moment for the Sixers in their home opener would be the handshake and dance between Embiid and James during pregame introductions.

The NBA might have something to say about that, if the league office determines James made one too many hip pumps there. Officials may have to check with the fictional Hingle McCringleberry or real Jamaal Williams .

Poor VJ Edgecombe was also left hanging by Embiid. He had to console himself with 11 points, 7 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 steals.

The 76ers continue their homestand by hosting the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday, while the Cavaliers host the Brooklyn Nets for their home opener.

articles.title: LeBron se estrena en Filadelfia con la mayor remontada de su carrera
articles.standfirst: Los Sixers, con su quinteto estelar a pleno rendimiento, levantan 29 puntos a los Cavaliers
articles.summary: Los Sixers, con su quinteto estelar a pleno rendimiento, levantan 29 puntos a los Cavaliers
articles.body: Uno de los mejores jugadores de la historia y una de las grandes estrellas de la NBA actual se estrenaban con los Sixers en casa. El debut en Filadelfia de LeBron James y Jaylen Brown ya era histórico en sí. Por eso las entradas habían alcanzado precios superiores a los 4.000 dólares. Bien invertidos, pensarán ahora quienes los pagaron. Porque los dos protagonistas y el resto del quinteto titular de su equipo convirtieron la noche en algo memorable. "Una de las cinco mejores desde que estoy", dijo Joel Embiid, que lleva 13 años en el equipo. Levantaron 29 puntos a los Cavaliers (40-69) para terminar ganando por 114-106. Se trata de la mayor remontada en la carrera de LeBron, y hablamos de alguien que vive su vigesimocuarta temporada en la NBA y ha disputado más de 1.600 encuentros, y la más grande de la franquicia en los últimos 30 años, desde que existe el jugada a jugada. Para conseguir la gesta, los Sixers se apoyaron en su quinteto titular. La pléyade de estrellas que pueden alinear de inicio metió 105 de los 114 puntos de su equipo: 32 de Tyrese Maxey, 24 de Joel Embiid, 21 de Jaylen Brown, 17 de LeBron James y 11 de VJ Edgecombe. Con semejante arsenal, no necesitaron más que una rotación de nueve jugadores. Sí les hará falta durante el resto de la temporada, cuando comiencen los descansos y los problemas físicos. En los dos primeros partidos, los Sixers ya han lanzado un aviso a la NBA. Han derrotado a los Knicks en el Madison y han firmado una remontada histórica ante los Cavaliers. Fueron, además de posibles destinos de LeBron cuando meditaba su futuro, los dos equipos finalistas de la Conferencia Este la temporada pasada y que están llamados también a colocarse arriba en la actual. Los de Cleveland son el primer equipo en la historia de la NBA que pierde un partido en su noche inaugural cuando iba ganando por más de 20 puntos al descanso. Desde el curso 84-85, el balance era de 65-0. A los visitantes no les bastaron los 32 puntos y 10 rebotes de Donovan Mitchell, ni el 18+8 de Evan Mobley, ni los 16 y cinco asistencias de James Harden. Se vinieron abajo en la segunda parte y en el último cuarto encajaron un demoledor 32-16 que culminó la heroicidad de los Sixers. El exmadridista Mario Hezonja tuvo un desacertado reestreno en la NBA 11 años después y tras seis sin estar en la Liga: hizo 10 puntos en 19 minutos, pero con 5/13 en tiros incluidos 0/5 en triples. Una canasta de Mitchell a falta de 1:12 para el descanso puso un marcador para frotarse los ojos: 40-69. Los Sixers, en el debut de sus estrellas, caía por 29. Se escucharon incluso silbidos para un equipo que se plantó al intermedio con 4/15 en triples y 14 pérdidas de balón. Pero el equipo se conjuró en el vestuario y mutó en la segunda mitad. Para empezar, mayor intensidad. Tanta que Maxey y Harden tuvieron que ser superados después de un pique en el último cuarto, cuando los Cavaliers ya sentían la respiración de su rival en el cogote (82-90). En el cuarto acto, los de Filadelfia no dieron opción. Dejaron secos a los Cavaliers durante casi cinco minutos. En mitad de un parcial de 15-0 liderado por Maxey, Brown y Embiid se obró la remontada. La consumó el pívot con una canasta a falta de 6:54 para el final: 96-95. La renta de los locales llegó hasta el +9 con el 104-95. El triunfo no se les iba a escapar. "Todo el año. Sólo tenemos que manejar bien la adversidad", dijo Jaylen Brown para resumir una noche histórica.

articles.title: Knicks Assistants Reportedly Haven't Gotten NBA Championship Rings, MSG Employees Tricked by Email
articles.summary: New York Knicks assistant coaches didn't receive their championship rings during the team's ceremony at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night, according to Joe Vardon of The Athletic.
articles.body:
New York Knicks assistant coaches didn't receive their championship rings during the team's ceremony at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night, according to Joe Vardon of The Athletic.

Per Vardon, assistants were informed earlier on Tuesday that they would not be getting their rings that evening and would obtain them at a later date instead. The Oklahoma City Thunder similarly didn't give out rings to assistants and some executives on opening night following the organization's 2025 title, although other organizations did.

Vardon also reported that many longtime employees at Madison Square Garden won't receive Knicks rings, although an email was previously sent to a "long list" of MSG staff members in which they were asked to choose the design of their "complimentary employee championship ring."

The email turned out to be a phishing test that MSG sent to see if employees would click, per Vardon. If they did, they did not get to choose any design and were required to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class instead.

Knicks players were individually presented with their championship jewelry before raising a banner to commemorate their title in a ceremony prior to a season-opening matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers.

New York previously defeated the San Antonio Spurs in five games during the 2026 NBA Finals, ending the organization's 53-year championship drought.

articles.title: LeBron James Praises 76ers Crowd, Admits Boos Were 'Deserved' Before Historic Comeback vs. Cavs
articles.summary: LeBron James got the full Philadelphia experience on Thursday night during the 76ers' 114-106 home-opening win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
articles.body:
LeBron James got the full Philadelphia experience on Thursday night during the 76ers' 114-106 home-opening win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Philly fans weren't pleased during a rough first half, when the team trailed by as many as 29 points and boos rained down. But the atmosphere was incredibly charged during the team's second-half comeback, and James enjoyed both sides of the experience.

"It was everything that I dreamed of and more," he told reporters . "The boos, that was amazing. We deserved it. And then we got the cheers and almost blew the roof off this thing tonight in a good way. So that was a hell of a night."

James wasn't the only one to point out how electric the atmosphere was on Thursday night:

The Sixers are only two games into the season, but wins over the New York Knicks and Cavaliers has folks in Philly feeling pretty good. Expect Xfinity Mobile Arena to be rocking this season.

articles.title: LeBron James laughs off President Trump's criticism about national anthem, Sixers coach calls it 'outside noise'
articles.summary: This isn't the first time LeBron James and Donald Trump have had a disagreement.
articles.body:
LeBron James does not seem to mind that the president of the United States is mad at him.

The Philadelphia 76ers star drew some attention for his behavior during the national anthem at his team's season-opener against the New York Knicks on Tuesday. As "The Star Spangled Banner" played, James went through rotational exercises and his shooting motion while lined up with his teammates .

It was a small moment during a larger pregame ceremony at Madison Square Garden , but footage from the crowd began going viral Wednesday and drew the attention of President Donald Trump on Thursday.

Posting on Truth Social, Trump blasted the four-time NBA champion:

While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP

Trump continued to criticize James during a rally at Sioux City, Iowa, on Thursday night, calling James' exercises a "golf swing" and "a big scandal kind of story."

James and the Sixers did not appear bothered by the comments. Speaking before Thursday's game against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Sixers head coach Nick Nurse downplayed Trump's words as one more outside distraction for Philadelphia, which entered this season with championship expectations after the team added James and Jaylen Brown to a playoff-level core.

"I think that goes right in with other outside noise we've already had," Nurse said before the game. "I keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor. The focus that they've had and the intent and all the stuff like that has been outstanding."

Speaking after the game, a historic comeback win over the Cavaliers , James was also asked about Trump. His reaction was a quick chuckle, then a quick comment :

"Must have been a slow news day at the office. Slow news day at the office.

James avoided going through similar motions before the anthem Thursday, though he could definitely be seen swinging his hips at one point .

This is far from James and Trump's first run-in. Their animosity was most notable when James called Trump a "bum" over the president's attempt to rescind the NBA champion Golden State Warriors' White House invitation after it became clear Stephen Curry and Co. would not be attending.

James has been politically outspoken in the past, often in disagreement with Trump, and also endorsed all three of Trump's presidential opponents in the 2016, 2020 and 2024 elections.

articles.title: Knicks reportedly turned fake championship ring offers into cybersecurity lesson for employees
articles.summary: The Knicks' championship rings have produced some awkward stories.
articles.body:
There are surprisingly few constants when it comes to sports teams handing out championship rings.

We know a championship ring is going to be gaudy. We know the players who won that championship will get one. We know there will be some sort of ceremony. But beyond that, it's really up to the team how far they want to go with it, especially when it comes to the number of employees who actually get one.

That uncertainty has become relevant thanks to the New York Knicks' breakthrough.

The Athletic's Joe Vardon reports that in September, several Madison Square Garden employees received an email offering recipients a first glimpse at their championship rings, with two designs to choose from for their new jewelry:

"Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here," the email read. "(Employee name), this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you. "There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below."

"Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here," the email read.

"(Employee name), this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you.

"There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below."

Some number of employees clicked the link in the email. Instead of a ring, their reward was, reportedly, a mandatory cybersecurity class, as the email was an elaborate phishing test orchestrated to address Dolan's concerns about cybersecurity.

Making that situation even more bizarre is that many longtime Madison Square Garden employees, including some who work in the Knicks' business operations, reportedly won't be receiving rings at all.

Again, there is no set rule for which employees receive championship rings, but owners are often generous in that regard, though most employees receive toned-down rings in comparison to the diamond-encrusted monsters the players get. And the employees who don't get them usually aren't psychologically haunted by fake ring offers from their own company.

The coaching staff pretty much always get rings as well, but the Knicks reportedly differed from the norm as well in one respect.

The Knicks assistant coaches were all handed boxes clearly meant to hold the rings as stirring music played in Madison Square Garden. According to The Athletic, those boxes were empty.

The assistant coaches are expected to eventually receive those rings, but they weren't available Tuesday as the team is still reportedly going through the process of measuring ring sizes and placing orders.

The Athletic notes the assistants of the Oklahoma City Thunder didn't get their rings on opening night last year either. The Thunder just didn't pretend they had them during the ceremony .

Another difference between the Knicks' ring night and the Thunder's ring night was the presence of NBA commissioner Adam Silver — or, lack thereof in the Knicks' case. The NBA commissioner is usually on hand to address the crowd and present players with their rings, but Knicks great Walt Frazier was the one handing out rings on Tuesday.

Silver was relegated to a chair on the other side of the court, while the likes of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and Jon Bon Jovi stood behind presenter Mike Breen. Dolan and Silver are well-known to be at odds, and Silver's placement appears to be another way Dolan's presence was felt on a celebratory occasion for the Knicks.

images.caption: The Knicks are still working on getting their championship rings to the right people. (USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect / REUTERS)

articles.title: SGA's Streak Ends as Thunder Beat Nuggets, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Jokic, Chet, Murray, More
articles.summary: A pair of former MVPs matched up on Thursday as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder took on Nikola Jokić and the Denver Nuggets.
articles.body:
A pair of former MVPs matched up on Thursday as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder took on Nikola Jokić and the Denver Nuggets.

It was a slow night for both stars, but the Thunder walked away with a 96-84 win, improving to 2-0 after handing the Nuggets a loss in their season opener. Unfortunately for Gilgeous-Alexander, his 141-game streak with 20-plus points came to an end.

While the battle between Gilgeous-Alexander and Jokić was the storyline coming in, neither looked like their MVP selves.

Gilgeous-Alexander struggled to find his shot and didn't make a field goal until the second half. He finally got things going in the fourth quarter to help put the Nuggets away, but he couldn't avoid losing his impressive streak.

That led to Jalen Williams taking the reins on offense for most of the game.

There was also a lid on the basket for Jokić all game, as he shot a lackluster 5-of-19 from the field. Chet Holmgren's work clogging the paint didn't make things any easier for Jokić and the Nuggets' big men.

The Thunder and Nuggets have each had some of the best offenses in the NBA over the last few years, but the two teams are clearly still finding their shot early in the season.

OKC finished the game shooting 38 percent from the field and 26 percent from deep, while Denver shot 38 percent from the field and 27 percent from deep. The Nuggets also turned the ball over 22 times.

The Thunder ultimately snuck away with a win despite the cold night offensively, but both teams will be looking to improve when they meet again later this season.

articles.title: 'It's a good sign': 76ers stars overcome adversity together in historic comeback win
articles.summary: The Sixers' home opener was a tale of two halves that revealed a very raw and dangerous group.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — As Jaylen Brown thumped his chest and roared toward the 76ers faithful with five minutes remaining in regulation, the arena that earlier echoed with boos from the tough crowd was now filled with songs of admiration and adoration.

A heap of confused, dejected Cavaliers shuffled back to the bench, their 29-point, first-half lead gone. A group that had poked holes in the 76ers' defensive game plan through smart team basketball was succumbing to an entrapment of individuality, unable to get out of its own way.

On Thursday, the 76ers completed their largest comeback win in the play-by-play era, a true tale of two halves that ultimately depicted a very raw and dangerous group hell-bent on controlling its narrative.

"We were out of total sync to start the game," head coach Nick Nurse said following the 114-106 win . "We just couldn't get ourselves going for some reason. We started picking it up in the second half, switched things defensively and got in a better position."

Deconstructing this game — historical comebacks aside — it's clear Philadelphia's playmaking structure will be a fluid entity in the coming weeks (and maybe months). The first half featured all of the worst aspects that come with an assemblage of transcendent talent. Aside from some occasional movement on the perimeter, the ball seemed to stick a bit too much.

Some of that is attributed to Brown. He's never been particularly regarded as a connective tissue type relative to his usage , and on a new team it's understandable that the former Finals MVP would want to play himself into a role and rhythm. But oftentimes it came as a detriment to the group. Having LeBron James around should help clean up ball movement issues, but it's more important that those habits continue when he's not on the floor. (In 10 first-quarter possessions with James on the bench, the 76ers were a minus-8, with one assist and a pair of turnovers.)

The good news is that it's not solely attributable to selfishness. This is a relatively new relationship for half of the quartet and, in the opening minutes, it was apparent that each star was trying to empower the other with James acting as a centripetal force. Eventually, all roads led back to Tyrese Maxey (who finished with 32 points on 23 shots) — as they should — and the 76ers were all able to settle into a role.

It also helped that the more the ball was in Maxey's hands, the more apt Philly became at creating paint touches, taking advantage of Jarrett Allen's bench minutes and attacking Evan Mobley and Jordan Tyson. Once the game was settled, the stars were able to find phases of individual dominance to fortify their lead; Joel Embiid taking advantage of smaller matchups around the elbows, James catching and going on the wing, and Maxey and Brown getting into the teeth of the defense to cause general disruption.

(One area where Nurse might want to tinker with is his substitution patterns concerning Maxey and Brown. If the bulk of the offensive juice is to come from them, taking them both out and leaving James and Embiid surrounded with shooters sounds inventive in theory, but it's equivalent to taking a fish out of water.)

"It should flow organically like it did, especially in the second half," James said. "We should never have to put pressure on ourselves to feel like we have to do too much offensively. When a guy has a good rhythm, try to feed them. But it comes down to the system of the offense and doesn't look forced."

Where the game truly changed for the 76ers, and an area they should wholeheartedly lean into as their offense continues to come together, is their defensive point-of-attack aggression. Aside from the starters — who finished as a plus-18 in 17 minutes together — nearly every positive five-man pairing had Kentavious Caldwell-Pope on the floor. Reserve big Adem Bona also made the most of his 13 minutes, giving Philly a more agile and mobile big than Embiid, allowing the smaller guards to ramp up ball pressure, switch and blitz. Following the game, the Cavaliers spoke about some of those changes that caught them by surprise, resulting in 21 turnovers.

The fine line between making bold statements in October and creating data points for later is rather delicate, but this is an extremely intriguing 76ers team that should only continue to find stability as they spend more time with each other on the floor. Their star depth will allow the likes of James and Embiid to earn much-needed rest (neither played more than 35 minutes, which is what Nurse wants) and Maxey and Brown should be able to express themselves at all levels. There will be games where their star-studded structure is truly tested, but so far, they've handled the early, important tests and are growing in confidence and poise.

"That's how you handle adversity," Brown said. "It's not gonna be perfect. All year, we gotta be able to handle adversity well and we'll be alright. It's a good sign."

articles.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finishes with 17 points in Thunder home opener, ending 141-game streak of 20 points
articles.summary: It had been a very long time since Gilgeous-Alexander scored less than 20 points in a game.
articles.body:
Just two games into the 2026 season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's long-running scoring streak has come to an end. The Oklahoma City Thunder point guard scored 17 points in the team's home opener on Thursday, though the Thunder held on for a 96-84 win.

The performance broke an NBA record 141-game streak of Gilgeous-Alexander scoring 20 or more points in a game. The regular-season streak dates back nearly two years ago to Oct. 30, 2024, when Gilgeous-Alexander scored 18 points in a win over the San Antonio Spurs.

Gilgeous-Alexander was held to just two points in the first half on Thursday, going 0-for-7 from the field. He ramped things up in the second half, ending 6-for-19 on field-goal shooting.

For a moment, Gilgeous-Alexander seemed like he would be able to storm all the way back and preserve the streak: The two-time league MVP scored 10 points in the fourth quarter, capping it off with a big 3-pointer.

But with the Thunder's win pretty much locked up, Gilgeous-Alexander checked out of the game with less than two minutes remaining, falling just short of the 20-point mark.

Postgame, Gilgeous-Alexander said he was planning on going back out there, but saw the Nuggets had also taken out their starters, and decided he should honor that by not going back in.

"I feel like you always treat the game with respect," Gilgeous-Alexander said, via Clemente Almanza of OKC Thunder Wire . "God willing, I have many more games to start another streak, so."

In March, Gilgeous-Alexander's streak put him in the record books, as the guard passed Wilt Chamberlain for the longest-running 20-plus point streak in NBA history with his 127th game. Gilgeous-Alexander kept the streak going for the rest of the regular season, despite some close calls . He scored 32 in the Thunder's season opener on Tuesday.

Even with the streak coming to an end, it's long been proof of Gilgeous-Alexander's scoring efficiency. When looking at the stats , Gilgeous-Alexander has hit 20 points before the fourth quarter in most of his games. It's a streak that surpasses every other active player by a significant margin — let alone leaving 15 games between him and Chamberlain's mark.

The 28-year-old Gilgeous-Alexander will have a chance to start a new streak Sunday, as the Thunder host the Los Angeles Clippers.

articles.title: Shai renuncia a alargar una de las rachas de la NBA que parecen imbatibles
articles.standfirst: El base de los Thunder, vigente MVP, se queda por debajo de los 20 puntos por primera vez en dos años: 141 partidos consecutivos
articles.summary: El base de los Thunder, vigente MVP, se queda por debajo de los 20 puntos por primera vez en dos años: 141 partidos consecutivos
articles.body: Se rompió uno de esos récords de la NBA que parecen imbatibles. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, vigente MVP de la NBA, llevaba 141 partidos consecutivos anotando al menos 20 puntos. La última vez que no había llegado a esa cifra fue hace casi dos años, el 30 de octubre de 2024. En el estreno de la temporada de los Thunder, el base canadiense se quedó en 17. Y lo más llamativo es que renunció a mantener su racha. En la victoria sobre los Nuggets por 96-84, Shai tuvo una mala noche. No anotó en juego en toda la primera mitad (0/7), llegó al descanso con dos míseros tiros libres y su equipo cayendo 44-48. Al final del tercer cuarto llevaba siete puntos con 2/13 en tiros de campo incluido un paupérrimo 1/8 en triples. Pero entró en erupción en un momento dado del último periodo. Tratando de guiar a su equipo a la victoria, sumó 10 puntos con dos aciertos desde el arco, uno complicadísimo y otro para ponerse a tiro de alargar su récord. Después de ese triple, sin embargo, con 1:43 minutos por jugarse y 93-76 en el marcador, no salió del banquillo tras un tiempo muerto. Tenía tiempo de haber sumado los tres puntos que necesitaba, pero ni lo intentó. "Pidió salir del partido al final. Esa fue su sustitución. Tiene una tremenda clase como competidor", valoró el entrenador Mark Daigneault. “Habla de lo bien que mantiene la perspectiva”, dijo Jalen Williams. Una muestra de liderazgo hacia sus compañeros: la victoria está asegurada y lo demás da igual. Una distracción menos: intentar mantener esas rachas puede descentrar. El caso: 141 partidos seguidos con al menos 20 puntos. Una bestialidad. Los Thunder sumaron su segundo triunfo de la temporada aprovechando la explosión final de su estrella, pero también la energía que aporta Jalen Williams, el mejor anotador de los Thunder con 21 puntos. Chet Holmgren puso los rebotes, con 17, nueve de ellos ofensivos. Aday Mara también ayudó ahí. Sus tres capturas fueron en el aro de los Nuggets. Jugó 13 minutos y anotó dos puntos con 1/3 en tiros de campo, robó un balón y puso un tapón. Jugando ante Nikola Jokic, con el que se le compara por ser un pívot con gran capacidad de pase y una extraordinaria visión de juego, el español tuvo menos impacto que en su debut ante Victor Wembanyama. En sus dos primeros partidos en la NBA ya se ha enfrentado a dos referentes. Jokic estuvo tan desatinado como todo su equipo. Hizo 13 puntos, siete rebotes y cinco asistencias, pero chirrió el 5/19 en tiros de campo. Jamal Murray, otra pieza clave de Denver, estuvo aún peor: seis puntos con 2/11. Los Nuggets acabaron con un mal 8/30 en triples y sólo Aaron Gordon estuvo fino con 20 puntos con 3/4, aunque en el último cuarto hasta él se secó ante la intensidad de unos Thunder que volverán a ser una de las defensas más duras de la Liga.

articles.title: LeBron responde a Trump por criticar su comportamiento durante el himno
articles.standfirst: El alero de los Sixers vuelve a enzarzarse en una polémica con el presidente de Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El alero de los Sixers vuelve a enzarzarse en una polémica con el presidente de Estados Unidos
articles.body: LeBron James y Donald Trump se han vuelto a enzarzar en una polémica. El presidente de Estados Unidos criticó la actitud del jugador de los Sixers durante la interpretación del himno nacional antes del primer partido de la temporada en el Madison Square Garden ante los Knicks y ya ha recibido su respuesta. "Hoy no hay muchas noticias en la oficina", ironizó el alero sobre las polémicas que provoca el mandatario. Trump aseguró que LeBron debería "disculparse con todos esos grandes guerreros y héroes que murieron por la bandera estadounidense y por todo lo que representa nuestro país. Ya dije desde el principio que no sirve para nada, una vergüenza total". Esas fueron las palabras del presidente cuando vio que la estrella de la NBA no permanecía quieto durante la interpretación del himno sino que parecía practicar un golpe de golf y un tiro en suspensión mientras la mayoría de sus compañeros sí estaban inmóviles. Sin embargo, las críticas de Trump contrastan con su propio comportamiento en algunas ocasiones. En 2020, el Miami Herald publicó un vídeo en el que se veía al mandatario agitando las manos como si dirigiera una orquesta mientras sonaba el himno. Es una polémica más entre uno de los deportistas más célebres de Estados Unidos y el presidente del país. LeBron, activo en asuntos sociales, especialmente durante el movimiento 'Black Lives Matter', ha recibido muchas críticas de Trump: "Este es un país hermoso y nunca vamos a permitir que una sola persona dicte lo hermosos y poderosos que somos". "Sigo sabiendo lo que hago en la cancha y, obviamente, lo doy todo por el baloncesto, pero ahora mismo puedo tener un mayor impacto fuera de la cancha que dentro de ella. Quiero seguir inspirando a la gente con mi forma de jugar, pero hay muchas más cosas que puedo hacer fuera de la cancha para ayudar a formar a la gente, inspirarla, unirla y empoderarla", dijo LeBron en su día.

articles.title: "Doncic nunca ganará el MVP de la NBA"
articles.standfirst: La predicción del polémico Draymond Green
articles.summary: La predicción del polémico Draymond Green
articles.body: Desde su segundo año en la NBA, Luka Doncic ha estado en las quinielas para ganar el MVP. Seis veces ha sido elegido en el mejor quinteto de la temporada. Ha visto levantar el trofeo a Giannis Antetokounmpo, Nikola Jokic, Joel Embiid y, en las dos últimas ocasiones, a Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, pero él no lo ha conseguido. Y, según Draymond Green, no lo va a conseguir. El polémico jugador de los Warriors tiene un podcast en el que no se corta al hablar de ningún asunto. Esta vez opinó sobre Doncic, del que dijo que "nunca ganará el MVP. Este es el último año en que puede ganarlo". No es una crítica al base de los Lakers, al que reconoce su talento y condiciones, sino que habla de dar por hecho las cosas cuando se trata de algunas estrellas de la NBA. "Si pudiera promediar 34 puntos por partido, dirían: 'Ah, sí, por supuesto que Luka promedió 34 puntos por partido'. Ya sabemos que se supone que debe hacerlo, pero no se vería como si lo hiciera otro. Es como si la gente se cansara de eso", asegura. Y pone también como ejemplos a Jayson Tatum o la carrera de LeBron James: "No me digas que sólo debería tener cuatro premios MVP". En las carreras en que Doncic ha participado en busca del MVP se ha visto perjudicado por los problemas físicos. En las ocho temporadas completas que ha vivido en la NBA, sólo en dos de ellas, la de rookie y la 2023-24, ha conseguido alcanzar los 70 encuentros. El galardón se basa en estadísticas, en calidad, en éxito colectivo y en una continuidad que el base casi nunca ha disfrutado. Ahora que parece dedicar más tiempo al cuidado de su cuerpo podría tener más opciones. Tampoco le han acompañado las victorias. Estando en los Mavericks, su tope fueron 52 en una temporada regular. Llevó al equipo a una final de la NBA y a otra de Conferencia. En su primer año completo en los Lakers, el pasado, el equipo llegó a las 53, aunque él tuvo que compartir liderazgo con LeBron James y se quedó en sólo 64 partidos. Shai, Jokic y Victor Wembanyama terminaron por delante de él en las votaciones. Esta campaña, como gran referente del conjunto angelino, Doncic tratará de echar por tierra la predicción de Green.

articles.title: NBA: LeBron James enjoys dream home debut in 76ers comeback win over Cleveland Cavaliers
articles.summary: LeBron James says his home debut was "everything that I dreamed of and more" after the Philadelphia 76ers turned boos into cheers by overhauling a 29-point deficit to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106.
articles.body:
LeBron James says his home debut was "everything that I dreamed of and more" after the Philadelphia 76ers turned boos into cheers by overhauling a 29-point deficit to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106.

It is the largest comeback win of James' 24-season NBA career and also the largest comeback by the 76ers in the play-by-play era, which began in 1996-97.

Booed from the court after trailing 69-45 at half-time, Philadelphia took the lead for the first time with just under seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, with a spell of 15 unanswered points putting them 104-95 ahead.

Although the Cavaliers, one of James' three previous franchises, pulled it back to 106-102, the 76ers held firm having emphatically outscored their visitors 69-37 in the second half.

James contributed 17 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and three steals while fellow home debutant Jaylen Brown scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half, including 10 in the fourth quarter.

Tyrese Maxey top-scored for the Sixers with 32 points, with Joel Emiid adding 24.

"We got the boos. That was amazing and we deserved it. And then we got the cheers and almost blew the roof off this thing, in a good way. It was a hell of a night," said James, who joined the 76ers on a two-year contract.

The result caps off a thrilling start for James at his fourth franchise, after the Sixers defeated the New York Knicks 106-100 on the opening night of the season to spoil the defending champions' homecoming.

However, he also had to respond to criticism from President Donald Trump, who labelled the 41-year-old a "total disgrace" for not standing still during the national anthem before Tuesday's win over the Knicks.

"It must be a slow news day at the office," James said on Thursday night.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse said his side are used to tuning out such distractions, adding: "I think that goes right in with other outside noise we've already had.

"I keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor. The focus that they've had and the intent has been outstanding."

articles.title: LeBron James: Donald Trump accuses Philadelphia 76ers star of disrespecting US national anthem before NBA season opener
articles.summary: President Donald Trump accused NBA star LeBron James of disrespecting the US during Philadelphia’s opener against the New York Knicks, prompting James to hit back on Thursday, calling it a “slow news day in the office”
articles.body:
Trump shared a video on Truth Social of LeBron James appearing to practise a golf swing and take a jump shot during the national anthem before Philadelphia's season opener against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday.

"While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country!" Trump wrote, branding the NBA star a "TOTAL DISGRACE" and demanding he apologise to US military personnel who died serving their country.

Trump and James have been critical of each other for years, occasionally trading public swipes.

"It must be a slow news day at the office," he said after the Sixers completed an epic comeback to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 in Philadelphia. "Slow news day at the office."

James stood with his arms behind his back and head bowed as Boyz II Men performed the national anthem before tip-off. He was then introduced to a rapturous ovation from the crowd of around 20,000.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse had repeatedly stressed the importance of tuning out outside distractions since training camp began. However, just hours before Philadelphia's home opener, the team found itself dealing with one from the president.

"I think that goes right in with other outside noise we've already had," Nurse said before the game. "I keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor. The focus that they've had and the intent and all the stuff like that has been outstanding."

Trump, speaking Thursday night at a campaign rally in Sioux City, Iowa, reiterated his complaint.

"And what about LeBron James? Did you see that deal?" Trump said. 'No, he's doing, during the national anthem he's practicing his golf swing. I said what the hell is that. It's a big scandal kind of a story. I don't understand it."

Sixers record biggest comeback of LeBron's career

Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points and Joel Embiid had 24 to help LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers wipe out a 29-point deficit in their home opener for their biggest comeback since 1997 and stun the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 on Tuesday night.

James finished with 17 points and 10 rebounds in the biggest comeback victory of his career, while fellow newcomer Jaylen Brown added 21 points in a game that could prove difficult for the Sixers to surpass this season. Philadelphia had opened the campaign with wins over the NBA champion Knicks and Eastern Conference finalists Cavaliers.

The Sixers refused to go down without a fight and tensions nearly boiled over in the fourth quarter when Maxey and his former Philadelphia teammate James Harden went nose-to-nose before being separated. Maxey was relentless on defence and sparked a 15-0 run that put the Sixers in front, leaving the Cavaliers searching for answers.

Donovan Mitchell scored 32 points for the Cavs in their season opener.

James flirted in free agency with a third stint in Cleveland before he signed a two-year deal with the Sixers for the veteran minimum.

He won one of his four NBA titles with the Cavaliers and is trying to add a fifth ring in Philadelphia. The hype for the home opener was real, with tickets listed on secondary markets for around $4,000 (£2,987) in the lower bowl. The win against the Knicks only cranked up the enthusiasm for the first look in Philly at James and Brown - and they responded with an opener to remember.

The 41-year-old James had his moments, igniting the crowd with an uncontested two-handed dunk in the first half before adding another basket off a Maxey steal.

However, the Sixers struggled from beyond the arc, missing 11 of their 15 three-point attempts, while committing 14 turnovers in the first half - compared with just 12 across their entire win over the Knicks. The home crowd responded with a chorus of boos late in the second quarter.

Mitchell led the way with 22 points in the first half as the Cavaliers built a 29-point advantage. But that lead evaporated in the fourth quarter, with Embiid scoring seven consecutive points to cut the deficit to 96-95. Philadelphia then held on to the lead until the final buzzer to complete a historic comeback victory.

articles.title: ‘That’s not who I am…’-Carmelo Anthony’s refusal sheds light on his NBA exit
articles.summary: Carmelo Anthony has explained why he refused to embrace a bench role late in his NBA career, admitting he could not accept becoming a veteran mentor rather t...
articles.body:
Carmelo Anthony has explained why he refused to embrace a bench role late in his NBA career, admitting he could not accept becoming a veteran mentor rather than a leading player.

Accepting the supporting role can be tough for top stars, especially during the end of their careers.

The former New York Knicks star believes accepting that position could change how people remember him, a mindset that may have contributed to the difficult end of his playing career.

Anthony discussed the subject on his podcast, 7PM in Brooklyn , reflecting on the challenge of adjusting to a reduced role as a player's abilities decline.

Carmelo Anthony explains why he rejected a bench role

Speaking on his podcast, Anthony made clear that he respected veterans who accepted supporting roles but did not see himself following the same path.

He said: "I can't take a Taj Gibson role, and I respect somebody like Taj Gibson to the utmost. But for me to take that role, no, that's not who I am. I can't accept that. I don't want to accept that role."

Anthony also explained that he worried about how younger players would remember him if they only saw him as a bench player rather than the star he had been during his prime.

"Once you're seen in that light, that's who you are. Even if it's a kid who's seeing you in that position, that's the first thing that he's going to see, which is the last thing of you. So now that's the memory," he added.

His comments offer insight into the difficulties he faced towards the end of his career, particularly after his time with the Houston Rockets ended early amid questions about his attitude towards a reduced role.

Anthony later found a place with the Portland Trail Blazers, where he returned to a starting role, before eventually accepting a bench position with the Los Angeles Lakers.

However, opportunities became harder to find, and he ultimately left the NBA without securing the championship that had eluded him throughout his career.

Well, that makes him one of the best ever to never touch the championship.

The debate also highlights the challenge facing veteran stars as they age. LeBron James has shown a willingness to accept a smaller role in pursuit of team success, while Anthony's comments suggest that protecting his identity as a star was a major consideration.

Anthony remains involved in basketball through his work as a broadcaster and podcast host, giving him the opportunity to reflect on a career that brought both major success and a difficult final chapter.
